title: How to Manage a Business Blog: Tools for Planning, Writing, and Publishing
excerpt: The complete toolkit for running a business blog — from content calendars and drafting to scheduling and analytics.

content.text: A blog only works if you can run it consistently. Most businesses start strong, publish five posts, then stall because the process is messy.
The fix is a simple toolchain that covers four jobs: planning, writing, publishing, and measuring. Here's how to set it up.
Notion and Google Sheets are the two most common choices. Notion gives you a proper database with statuses. Sheets is free and everyone already knows it.

items: Columns for: title, keyword, status, publish date, author
Batch topics by theme so writing sessions stay focused

content.text: Google Docs is the workhorse: comments, suggestions, and version history make editing painless. Grammarly catches the obvious errors before a human has to.
If you use AI for drafts, treat it as a junior writer. It produces the first version; a human adds the voice, examples, and final judgment.
Keep a short style guide in the same folder as your calendar: tone, banned words, how you address the reader. It keeps every post sounding like the same brand.
WordPress powers a large share of business blogs and handles plugins, SEO, and scheduled publishing out of the box. Ghost is a cleaner, faster option focused purely on writing.
For businesses that want speed and zero maintenance, a custom site on a modern stack publishes with a simple push to the repository. No dashboard to log into, no updates to babysit.
Buffer and Hootsuite schedule social posts in advance. Meta Business Suite does it free for Facebook and Instagram. Mailchimp or Substack can turn each post into an email newsletter.

items: Write one week, schedule the next
Turn each post into three social snippets
Send the newsletter the day the post goes live

content.text: Canva handles graphics. Pexels and Pixabay supply free stock photos. Keep a folder of brand templates so every post image looks consistent.
Google Analytics 4 shows which posts bring traffic. Google Search Console shows which keywords you rank for. Check both once a month, then write more of what works.
A blog that is planned, published, and measured on a rhythm beats a brilliant blog that publishes whenever someone remembers.
Consistency is the strategy. The tools just make consistency possible.
